# http-client API reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/documentation.cjs. Do not edit. -->

Generic HTTP requests use the native host client with counted invocation state.

## SPFxHttpClientInfo

Native generic HTTP client and counted invocation/loading/error controls local to this hook.

### Imports

```ts
import type { SPFxHttpClientInfo } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import type { SPFxHttpClientInfo } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/hooks';
```

### Examples

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { SPFxHttpClientInfo, useSPFxHttpClient } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

function Example() {
  const http: SPFxHttpClientInfo = useSPFxHttpClient();
  console.log(http.isReady, http.error);
  return <span>{http.isReady ? 'Ready' : 'Unavailable'}</span>;
}
```

| Member | Type | Requirement | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SPFxHttpClientInfo.clearError` | `() => void` | Required, readonly | — | Clear the current error |
| `SPFxHttpClientInfo.client` | `HttpClient \| undefined` | Required, readonly | — | Native SPFx client, undefined until available or when service consumption/initialization fails. Direct client requests do not update hook loading/error state. |
| `SPFxHttpClientInfo.error` | `Error \| undefined` | Required, readonly | — | Error from the latest-started invoke call; each new call clears it. Older/client-obsolete completions cannot replace it. Direct client usage is not tracked. |

| `SPFxHttpClientInfo.isLoading` | `boolean` | Required, readonly | — | True while any invoke call for the current client remains pending; direct client usage is not tracked. |

#### SPFxHttpClientInfo.clearError (2)

##### Returns

No value; initialization/context errors remain separate.

#### SPFxHttpClientInfo.invoke (2)

##### Throws

- Error if client is not available
- Callback/request failures are normalized to Error, published when current, and rethrown. HTTP response.ok is not checked automatically.

##### Examples (2)

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { useSPFxHttpClient } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { HttpClient } from '@microsoft/sp-http';

function Example() {
  const { invoke, isReady, isLoading } = useSPFxHttpClient();
  const [result, setResult] = React.useState<unknown>();
  const [failure, setFailure] = React.useState<string>();
  const run = async () => {
    setFailure(undefined);
    try {
      const data = await invoke(client =>
        client.get('https://api.example.com/data', HttpClient.configurations.v1)
          .then(res => res.json())
      );
      setResult(data);
    } catch (failure) {
      setFailure(failure instanceof Error ? failure.message : String(failure));
    }
  };
  return <>
    <button disabled={!isReady || isLoading} onClick={() => void run()}>Load</button>
    {failure && <span role="alert">{failure}</span>}
    <pre>{JSON.stringify(result)}</pre>
  </>;
}
```

##### Type parameters

- `T`: Result produced by the supplied operation.

##### Parameters

- `fn`: Function that receives HttpClient and returns a promise

##### Returns (2)

Promise with the result

#### SPFxHttpClientInfo.isReady

##### Examples (3)

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { useSPFxHttpClient } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

import { HttpClient } from '@microsoft/sp-http';

function LoadButton() {
  const { isReady, invoke } = useSPFxHttpClient();
  const load = async () => {
    try {
      const data = await invoke(client => client.get('https://api.example.com/data', HttpClient.configurations.v1).then(response => response.json()));
      console.log(data);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(error);
    }
  };
  return <button disabled={!isReady} onClick={() => void load()}>Load</button>;
}
```

## useSPFxHttpClient

Accesses the SPFx HttpClient from ServiceScope. Direct client calls do not update hook state. invoke tracks all pending calls for its current client and publishes errors only from the latest-started call; obsolete completions still settle their promises. HTTP non-success responses must be checked by the callback; the hook does not inspect response.ok.

### Imports (2)

```ts
import { useSPFxHttpClient } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { useSPFxHttpClient } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/hooks';
```

### Use when

- an event or effect must issue a generic HTTP request with tracked async state.

### Throws (3)

- Missing SPFx provider.

### Examples (5)

#### Basic usage

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { useSPFxHttpClient } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

function ClientStatus() {
  const info = useSPFxHttpClient();
  return <span>{info.isReady ? 'Ready' : 'Unavailable'}</span>;
}
```

#### Weather with readiness failure and retry

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { useSPFxHttpClient } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { HttpClient } from '@microsoft/sp-http';

function WeatherWidget() {
  const { invoke, isLoading, error, clearError, isReady } = useSPFxHttpClient();
  const [weather, setWeather] = React.useState<{ main?: { temp?: number } }>();

  const loadWeather = () => {
    invoke(client =>
      client.get(
        'https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q=London&appid=YOUR_KEY',
        HttpClient.configurations.v1
      ).then(res => {
        if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Request failed: ${res.status}`);
        return res.json();
      })
    ).then(data => setWeather(data)).catch(() => undefined);
  };

  React.useEffect(() => {
    if (isReady) loadWeather();
  }, [isReady]);

  if (!isReady) return <p role="status">Initializing...</p>;
  if (isLoading) return <p role="status">Loading weather...</p>;
  if (error) return <div><p role="alert">{error.message}</p><button onClick={() => { clearError(); loadWeather(); }}>Retry</button></div>;

  return <div>Temperature: {weather?.main?.temp}°K</div>;
}
```

#### Post a webhook with invocation state

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { useSPFxHttpClient } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { HttpClient } from '@microsoft/sp-http';

function SlackNotifier() {
  const { invoke, isLoading, isReady } = useSPFxHttpClient();

  const sendNotification = (message: string) => {
    invoke(client =>
      client.post(
        'https://hooks.slack.com/services/YOUR/WEBHOOK/URL',
        HttpClient.configurations.v1,
        {
          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
          body: JSON.stringify({ text: message })
        }
      ).then(response => {
        if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Request failed: ${response.status}`);
        return response;
      })
    ).then(() => console.log('Notification sent')).catch(console.error);
  };

  return (
    <button onClick={() => sendNotification('Hello!')} disabled={!isReady || isLoading}>
      Send to Slack
    </button>
  );
}
```
